observational_context.quote: Cohort 1 consisted of nine patients with KRIT1 variants, two with CCM2 variants, two with PDCD10 variants, and eight with the mutation not detected (Table 1). In Table 1, clinical characteristics and imaging findings are described according to All, KRIT1, CCM2, PDCD10, Mutation detected, and Mutation not detected groups. The mean diagnosis ages of the overall and the last brain MRI were 36.8 (standard deviation, SD 18.5) and 45.0 (SD 18.5) years old, respectively. There was a slight female predominance (male: female = 38.1:61.9). A total of 90.5% of the patients were symptomatic, and seizures were the most common manifestation. Moreover, the mean age of seizure onset was 34.5 (SD 19.5) years. CASH occurred in 52.4% of the patients overall; the mean age of CASH was 29.4 (SD 18.8) years old, and the mean number of CASH events was 1.8 (SD 1.3). Overall, 33.3% of the patients underwent surgery for CASH or enlarged symptomatic CCM lesions. A total of 42.9% of the overall patients had a family history. However, the rate was inaccurate because the family history of CCM was usually obtained by history taking. Meanwhile, the lesions were distributed over various locations. The frequencies were lower in the basal ganglia (9.5%) and thalamus (42.9%) than in the other sites.

observational_context.section: Body / Result / Detailed clinical, genetic data, and age-related disease burden of gene-confirmed FCCM patients
observational_context.quote: We investigated the detailed clinical and genetic information of the gene-confirmed FCCM individuals, including the proband and family members. (Table 2) The family members of one patient with a KRIT1 variant (K7), and two patients with PDCD10 variants (P1 and P2), received genetic testing, and four family members with the same variant as the proband were detected. Furthermore, these family members had CCM lesions confirmed by brain MRI. Two patients (K3 and P2) had spinal CM, and one (C1) had cutaneous CM. Among the probands with mutations detected, six experienced CASH. Two patients experienced recurrent symptomatic hemorrhage and severe neurological sequelae. In the KRIT1 variant group, two patients (22.2%) had splice-site mutations, and the others had protein-truncating variants. (Table S1) All of the mutations were null. The CCM2 group comprised one patient with a nonsense mutation and one with a missense mutation. The PDCD10 group included one patient with a nonsense mutation and one with a splice-site mutation. Interestingly, five novel variants and one novel variant were confirmed in KRIT1 and PDCD10, respectively. Four patients with KRIT1 variants had a history of tumor or a current tumor. One patient (K3) presented with headache and neck pain. Brain and spine MRI demonstrated CCM and spinal CM. At the age of 52 years, a follow-up spine MRI revealed an increased size and prominent heterogeneous enhancement of T2 high signal intensity around the CM in the thoracic spinal cord. The neuroradiologist suggested the possibility of CM with a recent hemorrhage and tumorous condition. The surgical biopsy exhibited diffuse midline glioma, classified as WHO grade IV.

LOF in CCM genes and GOF in MAP3K3 are mutually exclusive, and the researchers suggested that CCM complexes suppress the activity of MEKK3.
